# Data input & processing and initialization of CellChat object
```{r input_data}
ptm = Sys.time()
# Prepare required input data for CellChat analysis
seurat_object <- readRDS(params$seurat_integrated)
Idents(seurat_object) <- "renamed_cluster"
table(seurat_object$renamed_cluster)
table(seurat_object$sample)
#levels(seurat_object)

# Chow dataset
seurat_object_Chow <- subset(seurat_object, subset = sample == "Chow")
# HFSC dataset
seurat_object_HFSC <- subset(seurat_object, subset = sample == "HFSC")
seurat_object_Chow
seurat_object_HFSC
```

# **Chow
```{r chow_dir}
data_dir_chow <- file.path(params$output_dir, "data/chow", Sys.Date())
results_dir_chow <- file.path(params$output_dir, "results/chow", Sys.Date())

invisible(mapply(
  FUN = dir.create,
  list(data_dir_chow, results_dir_chow),
  MoreArgs = list(recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
))
```

```{r Chow_input}
data.input <- seurat_object_Chow@assays$RNA$counts

dim(data.input)
meta = seurat_object_Chow@meta.data
meta = meta[colnames(data.input),]
meta = data.frame(row.names = rownames(meta),celltype=meta$renamed_cluster) # create a dataframe of the cell labels

# Create a CellChat object
cellchat_Chow <- createCellChat(object = data.input, meta = meta, group.by = "celltype")
cellchat_Chow@meta$samples <- "vWAT"

#cellchat_Chow <- setIdent(cellchat_Chow, ident.use = "labels") # set "labels" as default cell identity
levels(cellchat_Chow@idents) # show factor levels of the cell labels
groupSize <- as.numeric(table(cellchat_Chow@idents)) # number of cells in each cell group

# Set the ligand-receptor interaction database
CellChatDB <- CellChatDB.mouse
showDatabaseCategory(CellChatDB)
# Show the structure of the database
dplyr::glimpse(CellChatDB$interaction)
# use a subset of CellChatDB for cell-cell communication analysis
CellChatDB.use <- subsetDB(CellChatDB, search = "Secreted Signaling", key = "annotation") # use Secreted Signaling, the other three are `Cell-Cell Contact`,`ECM-Receptor`, `Non-protein Signaling`.
# Only uses the Secreted Signaling from CellChatDB v1
#  CellChatDB.use <- subsetDB(CellChatDB, search = list(c("Secreted Signaling"), c("CellChatDB v1")), key = c("annotation", "version"))
# use all CellChatDB except for "Non-protein Signaling" for cell-cell communication analysis
# CellChatDB.use <- subsetDB(CellChatDB)
# use all CellChatDB for cell-cell communication analysis
# CellChatDB.use <- CellChatDB # simply use the default CellChatDB. We do not suggest to use it in this way because CellChatDB v2 includes "Non-protein Signaling" (i.e., metabolic and synaptic signaling). 
# set the used database in the object
cellchat_Chow@DB <- CellChatDB.use

# Preprocessing the expression data for cell-cell communication analysis
cellchat_Chow <- subsetData(cellchat_Chow) # This step is necessary even if using the whole database
future::plan("multisession", workers = 4) # do parallel
cellchat_Chow <- identifyOverExpressedGenes(cellchat_Chow)
cellchat_Chow <- identifyOverExpressedInteractions(cellchat_Chow)
cellchat_Chow@data

dim(data.input)
length(labels)
execution.time = Sys.time() - ptm
print(as.numeric(execution.time, units = "secs"))
```

# I. Inference of cell-cell communication network
```{r CCC_network}
# Compute the communication probability and infer cellular communication network
ptm = Sys.time()
cellchat_Chow <- computeCommunProb(cellchat_Chow, type = "triMean")
cellchat_Chow <- filterCommunication(cellchat_Chow, min.cells = 10)

# Extract the inferred cellular communication network as a data frame
df.net <- subsetCommunication(cellchat_Chow) # returns a data frame consisting of all the inferred cell-cell communications at the level of ligands/receptors. Set slot.name = "netP" to access the the inferred communications at the level of signaling pathways
# df.net <- subsetCommunication(cellchat_Chow, sources.use = c(1,2), targets.use = c(4,5)) # gives the inferred cell-cell communications sending from cell groups 1 and 2 to cell groups 4 and 5.
# df.net <- subsetCommunication(cellchat_Chow, signaling = c("WNT", "TGFb")) # gives the inferred cell-cell communications mediated by signaling WNT and TGFb.

# Infer the cell-cell communication at a signaling pathway level
cellchat_Chow <- computeCommunProbPathway(cellchat_Chow)

# Calculate the aggregated cell-cell communication network
cellchat_Chow <- aggregateNet(cellchat_Chow)
execution.time = Sys.time() - ptm
print(as.numeric(execution.time, units = "secs"))

ptm = Sys.time()
groupSize <- as.numeric(table(cellchat_Chow@idents))

par(mfrow = c(1,2), xpd=TRUE)
#netVisual_circle(cellchat_Chow@net$count, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, label.edge= F, title.name = "Number of interactions")
#netVisual_circle(cellchat_Chow@net$weight, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, label.edge= F, title.name = "Interaction weights/strength")

pdf(file.path(results_dir_chow,'Number of interactions.pdf'), width = 5, height = 6)
netVisual_circle(cellchat_Chow@net$count, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, label.edge= F, title.name = "Number of interactions")
dev.off()

pdf(file.path(results_dir_chow,'Interaction weights and strength.pdf'), width = 5, height = 6)
netVisual_circle(cellchat_Chow@net$weight, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, label.edge= F, title.name = "Interaction weights/strength")
dev.off()

mat <- cellchat_Chow@net$weight
plots_list <- list()
for (i in 1:nrow(mat)) {
  mat2 <- matrix(0, nrow = nrow(mat), ncol = ncol(mat), dimnames = dimnames(mat))
  mat2[i, ] <- mat[i, ]
  png(filename = sprintf('./CCC/results/chow/2024-10-05/%s_signaling.png',rownames(mat)[i]), width = 5, height = 5,units="in",res=500)
  p <- netVisual_circle(mat2, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, edge.weight.max = max(mat), title.name = rownames(mat)[i])
  print(p)
  dev.off()
  plots_list[[i]] <- p
}

```

# II. Visualization of cell-cell communication network
```{r visualization}
cellchat_Chow@netP$pathways
#[1] "COMPLEMENT" "SEMA3"      "CCL"        "GAS"        "FGF"        "ANGPTL"     "MIF"       
#[8] "GALECTIN"   "BMP"        "CXCL"       "PDGF"       "CHEMERIN"   "PROS"       "CSF"       
#[15] "IGF"        "WNT"        "VEGF"       "TGFb"       "PERIOSTIN"  "ncWNT"      "EDN"       
#[22] "ANNEXIN"    "VISFATIN"   "ANGPT"      "GRN"        "IL1"        "EGF"        "IGFBP"     
#[29] "LIFR"       "RANKL"      "TWEAK"      "IL2"        "PTPR"       "APRIL"      "SLIT"      
#[36] "PLAU"       "NT"            

pathways.selected <- c("COMPLEMENT","CCL","ANGPTL","MIF","TGFb")

pathways.show <- c("COMPLEMENT") 
# pathways.show <- c("CCL")
# pathways.show <- c("SEMA3")

# grouping cell clusters into immune or non-immune cell
levels(cellchat_Chow@idents)
group.cellType <- c("non_immune_cell","immune_cell","immune_cell","non_immune_cell","immune_cell","non_immune_cell","immune_cell","non_immune_cell","immune_cell") 
names(group.cellType) <- levels(cellchat_Chow@idents)

# Loop for Chord diagram
for (pathways.show in pathways.selected) {
  pdf(sprintf("./CCC/results/chow/2024-10-05/%s_chord.pdf",pathways.show), width = 6, height = 6)
  par(mfrow=c(1,1),xpd=TRUE)
  netVisual_aggregate(cellchat_Chow, signaling = pathways.show, group = group.cellType,
                      layout = "chord", title.name = paste0(pathways.show, " signaling network"))
  dev.off()
} 
```

```{r CCC_Complement_Chow}
netVisual_individual(cellchat_Chow, signaling = pathways.show, pairLR.use = LR.show, layout = "chord")
dev.off()

# Access all the signaling pathways showing significant communications
pathways.show.all <- cellchat_Chow@netP$pathways
# check the order of cell identity to set suitable vertex.receiver
print(levels(cellchat_Chow@idents))
# [1] "ASPC"             "B Cell"           "Dendritic Cell"   "Endothelial Cell" "Macrophage"      
# [6] "Mesothelial Cell" "Neutrophil"       "T Cell"  

vertex.receiver = seq(1,4)
for (i in 1:length(pathways.show.all)) {
  # Visualize communication network associated with both signaling pathway and individual L-R pairs
  netVisual(cellchat_Chow, signaling = pathways.show.all[i], vertex.receiver = vertex.receiver, layout = "hierarchy")
  # Compute and visualize the contribution of each ligand-receptor pair to the overall signaling pathway
  gg <- netAnalysis_contribution(cellchat_Chow, signaling = pathways.show.all[i])
  ggsave(filename=paste0("./CCC/results/chow/2024-10-04/L-R/", pathways.show.all[i], "_L-R_contribution.pdf"), plot=gg, width = 5, height = 5, units = 'in', dpi = 300)
}

# Visualize cell-cell communication mediated by multiple ligand-receptors or signaling pathways
# (A) Bubble plot
# (1) show all the significant interactions (L-R pairs) from some cell groups (defined by 'sources.use') to other cell groups (defined by 'targets.use')
levels(cellchat_Chow@idents)
netVisual_bubble(cellchat_Chow, sources.use = 5, targets.use = c(1:8), remove.isolate = FALSE)
# (2) show all the significant interactions (L-R pairs) associated with certain signaling pathways
netVisual_bubble(cellchat_Chow, sources.use = 5, targets.use = c(1:8), signaling = c("CCL","CXCL"), remove.isolate = FALSE)

pdf("./CCC/results/chow/2024-10-04/Bubble_L-R_ASPC_ANGPTL_contribution.pdf", width = 10, height = 5)
netVisual_bubble(cellchat_Chow, sources.use = c(1,4,5), targets.use = c(1,2,4,8,3,5,6,7), pairLR.use = pairLR.use, remove.isolate = TRUE)
dev.off()

# (B) Chord diagram
# show all the significant interactions (L-R pairs) from some cell groups (defined by 'sources.use') to other cell groups (defined by 'targets.use')
# show all the interactions sending from Inflam.FIB
netVisual_chord_gene(cellchat_Chow, sources.use = 5, targets.use = c(1,2,4,8), lab.cex = 0.5,legend.pos.y = 30)
# show all the significant interactions (L-R pairs) associated with certain signaling pathways
netVisual_chord_gene(cellchat_Chow, sources.use = c(1,2,3,4), targets.use = c(5:11), signaling = c("CCL","CXCL"),legend.pos.x = 8)
# show all the significant signaling pathways from some cell groups (defined by 'sources.use') to other cell groups (defined by 'targets.use')
netVisual_chord_gene(cellchat_Chow, sources.use = c(1,2,3,4), targets.use = c(5:11), slot.name = "netP", legend.pos.x = 10)

# Plot the signaling gene expression distribution using violin/dot plot
plotGeneExpression(cellchat_Chow, signaling = "CXCL", enriched.only = TRUE, type = "violin")

print(as.numeric(execution.time, units = "secs"))
#> [1] 1002.769

# Plot without enriched
plotGeneExpression(cellchat_Chow, signaling = "CXCL", enriched.only = FALSE)
execution.time = Sys.time() - ptm
```

# III: Systems analysis of cell-cell communication network
To facilitate the interpretation of the complex intercellular communication networks, CellChat quantitively measures networks through methods abstracted from graph theory, pattern recognition and manifold learning.
## Identify signaling roles (e.g., dominant senders, receivers) of cell groups as well as the major contributing signaling
```{r CCC_network}
ptm = Sys.time()
# (A) Compute and visualize the network centrality scores
pathways.show <- "COMPLEMENT"
# Compute the network centrality scores
cellchat_Chow <- netAnalysis_computeCentrality(cellchat_Chow, slot.name = "netP") # the slot 'netP' means the inferred intercellular communication network of signaling pathways
# Visualize the computed centrality scores using heatmap, allowing ready identification of major signaling roles of cell groups
for(pathways.show in pathways.selected) {
    png(filename = sprintf("./CCC/results/chow/2024-10-05/%s_centrality_scores.png",pathways.show), 
        width = 5, height = 3, units = "in", res = 500)
    netAnalysis_signalingRole_network(cellchat_Chow, signaling = pathways.show, width = 8, height = 2.5, font.size = 10)
    dev.off()
}
# (B) Visualize dominant senders (sources) and receivers (targets) in a 2D space
# Signaling role analysis on the aggregated cell-cell communication network from all signaling pathways
gg1 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter(cellchat_Chow)
#> Signaling role analysis on the aggregated cell-cell communication network from all signaling pathways
# Signaling role analysis on the cell-cell communication networks of interest
gg2 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter(cellchat_Chow, signaling = c("COMPLEMENT", "CCL"))
#> Signaling role analysis on the cell-cell communication network from user's input
gg1 + gg2
ggsave("./CCC/results/chow/2024-10-05/netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter.pdf", gg2, width = 5, height = 4)

gg1 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter(cellchat_Chow,title = "All signaling pathways", 
                                         label.size = 3, dot.alpha = 0.5)
gg2 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter(cellchat_Chow, signaling = "COMPLEMENT", title = "COMPLEMENT signaling pathway",
                                         label.size = 3, dot.alpha = 0.5)
gg3 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter(cellchat_Chow, signaling = "CCL", title = "CCL signaling pathway",
                                         label.size = 3, dot.alpha = 0.5)
gg1 + gg2 + gg3
ggsave("./CCC/results/chow/2024-10-05/netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter_3.pdf", width = 12, height = 4)

# (C) Identify signals contributing the most to outgoing or incoming signaling of certain cell groups
# Signaling role analysis on the aggregated cell-cell communication network from all signaling pathways
pathways.show <- c("COMPLEMENT","SEMA3","CCL","GAS","FGF","ANGPTL","MIF","GALECTIN","BMP","CXCL",
                   "PDGF","CHEMERIN","PROS","CSF","IGF","WNT","VEGF","TGFb","PERIOSTIN","ncWNT")
pdf("./CCC/results/chow/2024-10-05/outgoing_incoming_rank.pdf", width = 8, height = 8) # width = 7,height = 8
ht1 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_heatmap(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "outgoing", signaling = pathways.show, width = 4,height = 6)
ht2 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_heatmap(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "incoming", signaling = pathways.show, width = 4,height = 6)
ht1 + ht2
dev.off()
# Signaling role analysis on the cell-cell communication networks of interest

# Inflammatory Mediators:
## CCL and CXCL: These chemokines attract immune cells to the site of atherosclerotic lesions, contributing to inflammation.
## IL1: Promotes inflammation, which is central to atherosclerosis development.
## TNF-related molecules like TWEAK: Involved in inflammation and modulating vascular cell functions.
## MIF (Macrophage Migration Inhibitory Factor): Has roles in immune response regulation and is linked to atherosclerosis due to its pro-inflammatory effects.

# Growth Factors and Related Molecules:
## PDGF: Promotes smooth muscle cell proliferation and migration, crucial in plaque stability.
## FGF: Involved in cell growth and angiogenesis, can influence vascular repair and plaque stability.
## VEGF: Important for angiogenesis but also contributes to vascular permeability and inflammation.
## TGFb: Has complex roles including matrix formation, cellular migration, and potentially stabilizing plaques through fibrous cap formation.
## Lipid Metabolism and Adipokines:
## ANGPTL (Angiopoietin-like Proteins): Involved in lipid metabolism and inflammation.
## VISFATIN: An adipokine that may be linked to insulin resistance and inflammation in atherosclerosis.

# Extracellular Matrix and Cell Adhesion:
## SPP1 (Osteopontin): Plays roles in cell recruitment, adhesion, and survival within atherosclerotic plaques.
## PERIOSTIN: Influences collagen deposition and fibrous cap integrity.

#Other Signaling Pathways:
## WNT and ncWNT (non-canonical WNT signaling): Involved in the regulation of vascular cell function and potentially in the development of vascular diseases like atherosclerosis.
## BAFF: Known for its role in B-cell survival but also linked to autoimmune responses and inflammation in atherosclerosis.
## APRIL: Similar to BAFF, involved in immune regulation and may contribute to inflammatory processes in atherosclerosis.

#These molecules represent just a portion of the complex network of cellular interactions and signaling pathways involved in atherosclerosis. Each plays a role in different stages of the disease, from the initial development of fatty streaks to the progression of mature plaques and potential plaque rupture.

pdf("./CCC/results/chow/2024-10-05/Inflammatory_Mediators_rank.pdf",width = 8, height = 4)
ht1 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_heatmap(cellchat_Chow, signaling = c("CCL", "CXCL","MIF", "IL1","TWEAK"), 
                                         width = 4,height = 5*unit(3, "mm"), pattern = "outgoing")
ht2 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_heatmap(cellchat_Chow, signaling = c("CCL", "CXCL","MIF", "IL1","TWEAK"), 
                                         width = 4,height = 5*unit(3, "mm"), pattern = "incoming")
ht1 + ht2
dev.off()

pdf("./CCC/results/chow/2024-10-05/Growth_Factors_rank.pdf",width = 8, height = 4)
ht1 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_heatmap(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "outgoing",
                                        signaling = c("VEGF", "FGF","PDGF","TGFb"),
                                        width = 4, height = 4*unit(3, "mm"))
ht2 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_heatmap(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "incoming",
                                        signaling = c("VEGF", "FGF","PDGF","TGFb"),
                                        width = 4, height = 4*unit(3, "mm"))
ht1 + ht2
dev.off()

pdf("./CCC/results/chow/2024-10-05/Lipid_Metabolism_rank.pdf",width = 8, height = 4)
ht1 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_heatmap(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "outgoing",
                                        signaling = c("ANGPTL", "VISFATIN"),
                                        width = 4, height = 2*unit(3, "mm"))
ht2 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_heatmap(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "incoming",
                                        signaling = c("ANGPTL", "VISFATIN"),
                                        width = 4, height = 2*unit(3, "mm"))
ht1 + ht2
dev.off()
```

## Identify global communication patterns to explore how multiple cell types and signaling pathways coordinate together
In addition to exploring detailed communications for individual pathways, an important question is how multiple cell groups and signaling pathways coordinate to function. CellChat employs a pattern recognition method to identify the global communication patterns.
```{r pattern}
# (A) Identify and visualize outgoing communication pattern of secreting cells
library(NMF)
pdf("./CCC/results/chow/2024-10-05/patterns_selectK.pdf",width = 6, height = 4)
selectK(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "outgoing") # We run selectK to infer the number of patterns.
dev.off()
#Both Cophenetic and Silhouette values begin to drop suddenly when the number of outgoing patterns is 4.
nPatterns = 4
pdf("./CCC/results/chow/2024-10-05/patterns_outgoing.pdf", width = 8, height = 12)
cellchat_Chow <- identifyCommunicationPatterns(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "outgoing", k = nPatterns, width = 4, height = 10)
dev.off()
# river plot
library(ggalluvial)
pdf("./CCC/results/chow/2024-10-05/patterns_outgoing_river.pdf",width = 8, height = 6)
netAnalysis_river(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "outgoing")
dev.off()
# dot plot
pdf("./CCC/results/2024-07-23/patterns_outgoing_dot.pdf",width = 8, height = 4)
netAnalysis_dot(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "outgoing")
dev.off()

# (B) Identify and visualize incoming communication pattern of target cells
pdf("./CCC/results/chow/2024-10-05/patterns_selectK_incoming.pdf",width = 6, height = 4)
selectK(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "incoming") # We run selectK to infer the number of patterns.
dev.off()
nPatterns = 2
pdf("./CCC/results/chow/2024-10-05/patterns_incoming.pdf",width = 8, height = 12)
cellchat_Chow <- identifyCommunicationPatterns(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "incoming", k = nPatterns, width = 4, height = 10)
dev.off()
# river plot
pdf("./CCC/results/chow/2024-10-05/patterns_incoming_river.pdf",width = 8, height = 6)
netAnalysis_river(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "incoming")
dev.off()
# dot plot
pdf("./CCC/results/2024-07-23/patterns_incoming_dot.pdf",width = 8, height = 4)
netAnalysis_dot(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "incoming")
dev.off()
```

## Manifold and classification learning analysis of signaling networks
1. Functional similarity: High degree of functional similarity indicates major senders and receivers are similar, and it can be interpreted as the two signaling pathways or two ligand-receptor pairs exhibit similar and/or redundant roles. The functional similarity analysis requires the same cell population composition between two datasets.
2. Structural similarity: A structural similarity was used to compare their signaling network structure, without considering the similarity of senders and receivers.
```{r Manifold_classification}
# Identify signaling groups based on their functional similarity
cellchat <- computeNetSimilarity(cellchat, type = "functional")
reticulate::py_install(packages = 'umap-learn')
cellchat <- netEmbedding(cellchat, type = "functional")
cellchat <- netClustering(cellchat, type = "functional")
# Visualization in 2D-space
pdf("./CCC/results/2024-07-23/functional similarity.pdf",width = 8, height = 6)
netVisual_embedding(cellchat, type = "functional", label.size = 3.5)
dev.off()
pdf("./CCC/results/2024-07-23/functional similarity2.pdf",width = 8, height = 6)
netVisual_embeddingZoomIn(cellchat, type = "functional", nCol = 2)
dev.off()

# Identify signaling groups based on structure similarity
cellchat <- computeNetSimilarity(cellchat, type = "structural")
cellchat <- netEmbedding(cellchat, type = "structural")
#> Manifold learning of the signaling networks for a single dataset
cellchat <- netClustering(cellchat, type = "structural")
#> Classification learning of the signaling networks for a single dataset
# Visualization in 2D-space
pdf("./CCC/results/2024-07-23/structure similarity.pdf",width = 8, height = 6)
netVisual_embedding(cellchat, type = "structural", label.size = 3.5)
dev.off()
pdf("./CCC/results/2024-07-23/structure similarity2.pdf",width = 8, height = 6)
netVisual_embeddingZoomIn(cellchat, type = "structural", nCol = 2)
dev.off()
```

# I. Inference of cell-cell communication network
```{r CCC_network_hfsc}
# Compute the communication probability and infer cellular communication network
ptm = Sys.time()
cellchat_HFSC <- computeCommunProb(cellchat_HFSC, type = "triMean")
cellchat_HFSC <- filterCommunication(cellchat_HFSC, min.cells = 10)

# Extract the inferred cellular communication network as a data frame
df.net <- subsetCommunication(cellchat_HFSC) # returns a data frame consisting of all the inferred cell-cell 
# Infer the cell-cell communication at a signaling pathway level
cellchat_HFSC <- computeCommunProbPathway(cellchat_HFSC)

# Calculate the aggregated cell-cell communication network
cellchat_HFSC <- aggregateNet(cellchat_HFSC)
execution.time = Sys.time() - ptm
print(as.numeric(execution.time, units = "secs"))

ptm = Sys.time()
groupSize <- as.numeric(table(cellchat_HFSC@idents))

par(mfrow = c(1,2), xpd=TRUE)

pdf(file.path(results_dir_hfsc,'Number of interactions.pdf'), width = 5, height = 6)
netVisual_circle(cellchat_HFSC@net$count, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, label.edge= F, title.name = "Number of interactions")
dev.off()

pdf(file.path(results_dir_hfsc,'Interaction weights and strength.pdf'), width = 5, height = 6)
netVisual_circle(cellchat_HFSC@net$weight, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, label.edge= F, title.name = "Interaction weights/strength")
dev.off()

mat <- cellchat_HFSC@net$weight
plots_list <- list()
for (i in 1:nrow(mat)) {
  mat2 <- matrix(0, nrow = nrow(mat), ncol = ncol(mat), dimnames = dimnames(mat))
  mat2[i, ] <- mat[i, ]
  png(filename = sprintf('./CCC/results/hfsc/2024-10-07/%s_signaling.png',rownames(mat)[i]), width = 5, height = 5,units="in",res=500)
  p <- netVisual_circle(mat2, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, edge.weight.max = max(mat), title.name = rownames(mat)[i])
  print(p)
  dev.off()
  plots_list[[i]] <- p
}
```

# III: Systems analysis of cell-cell communication network
To facilitate the interpretation of the complex intercellular communication networks, CellChat quantitively measures networks through methods abstracted from graph theory, pattern recognition and manifold learning.
## Identify signaling roles (e.g., dominant senders, receivers) of cell groups as well as the major contributing signaling
